Grow With Stories

Choose the reading level that feels right for you. The stories grow with you, from your first English words to confident independent reading.

Grades 4–5

Little Seedling

Very simple English, short sentences and familiar words, with pictures, basic word meanings and easy questions. A gentle start before English becomes a bigger part of school.

→
Grades 6–7

Growing Sapling

Longer sentences and a growing vocabulary, with clear story structure. Word help in context and questions about what happens and why support what you learn in class.

→
Grades 8–10

Mighty Tree

Richer words, detailed storytelling and more about culture and meaning. Questions invite you to think deeply and read confidently on your own.

The platform follows this journey: it begins in Grades 4–5 with early English, continues through Grades 6–7 alongside classroom learning, and grows into confident independent reading in Grades 8–10.

    About us

    The people and the idea behind Kathaa Sangam.

    Who we are

    We are a group of students from the Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad, brought together by a shared interest in education, storytelling, and social impact.

    Our experiences span classrooms, community initiatives, and organisations such as Teach For India, Neev, and Ashoka, as well as social-impact initiatives at IIM Ahmedabad. Some of us have worked directly as teachers, fellows, or volunteers, giving us firsthand exposure to the opportunities and challenges of learning in diverse educational settings.

    These experiences inspired us to explore how storytelling could make language learning more engaging, accessible, and culturally meaningful.

    Through Kathaa Sangam, we hope to bring India’s rich storytelling traditions into children’s learning journeys while creating a free space for curiosity, creativity, and connection across cultures.

    Kathaa Sangam is a student project. The organisations named above are part of our own experiences; none of them has endorsed or sponsored this website.

    What we are building

    We are creating a free, multilingual digital repository of children’s folk stories from across India.

    Our aim is to bring together stories from different states, communities, and storytelling traditions in one accessible space.

    The platform will allow children to discover stories from across the country while developing their language skills, curiosity, and understanding of India’s cultural diversity.

    Why this matters

    🎁

    Accessible Learning

    The platform is intended to remain free, making stories and learning resources available to children regardless of their economic background.

    📖

    English Learning Through Storytelling

    We want children to develop English-language confidence naturally through stories rather than relying exclusively on conventional grammar exercises.

    🗣️

    Multilingual Learning

    Stories will be available in English and Hindi, with Gujarati versions added wherever feasible.

    🌈

    Celebrating Cultural Diversity

    Children should be able to explore different regions of India and understand the communities, traditions, and cultural contexts from which stories originate.

    🤝

    Building Connections Across Cultures

    By reading stories from different parts of the country, children can discover shared values, different perspectives, and the richness of India’s cultural heritage.

    💡

    Encouraging Critical Thinking

    The website should encourage children to reflect on stories, answer questions, share interpretations, and express their understanding creatively through writing and artwork.

    Sources & Acknowledgements

    Where every story and picture comes from.

    How we credit our work

    Folk stories are shared by many people over many years, and a traditional tale does not automatically make a particular book, retelling or picture free to reuse. We list each source and its permissions for every story, and we will not add a citation we have not checked.

    • Traditional or oral sources Stories passed on by storytellers, families and communities.
    • Published retellings Books or collections where a story was written down.
    • Adaptations Our simplified versions for the three reading levels.
    • Translations English, Hindi, and Gujarati or home-state-language versions, with translator credits.
    • Original illustrations Pictures made by named artists.
    • AI-assisted illustrations Pictures made with AI tools, always labelled as such.
